findings.title: Frozen dataclass uses evaluated-once default for queued timestamp
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls timezone.now() once at import time. Every AssignmentSource created via from_integration() without an explicit queued value therefore shares the same timestamp for the life of the process. The queued field cannot be used for ordering, debugging, or expiry. Fix is dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now).

findings.title: to_dict/from_dict not Celery-JSON safe, breaks outbound enqueue
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py, to_dict() returns asdict() including a raw datetime object for queued. In src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py sync_group_assignee_outbound passes that dict as assignment_source_dict to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs. Celery JSON serialization cannot serialize datetime, so any inbound assignment (which sets a source) will fail to enqueue outbound tasks to other integrations or raise serialization errors. Conversely from_dict() does cls(**input_dict) with no datetime parsing, so after JSON round-trip queued would be a string violating the declared type. Serialize queued to ISO string and parse it back.

findings.title: Outbound call passes undocumented assignment_source kwarg
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 59-61, the task calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source). The abstract contract in src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py for sync_assignee_outbound is (external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs) with no explicit assignment_source parameter, unlike sync_status_outbound which was updated. Any concrete IssueSyncIntegration subclass that overrides sync_assignee_outbound with an exact signature without **kwargs will raise TypeError on every outbound sync, breaking all assignee sync. Update the base signature to declare assignment_source explicitly.

findings.title: Loop suppression keyed only on integration_id over-suppresses and fail-opens
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 390, should_sync returns False when sync_source.integration_id equals org_integration.integration_id. AssignmentSource carries only integration_id, not organization_id. A single integration shared by multiple organizations will therefore suppress outbound sync for all organizations when only the originating organization should be suppressed. Separately, in src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py, AssignmentSource.from_dict returns None on malformed input, and should_sync(None) returns True, so any deserialization failure silently disables loop protection and reintroduces the cycle the PR fixes.
